projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
An analytics dashboard that unifies two data sources with a visualization layer.

Scope:
1. Customer CSV data processing — ingestion, validation, normalization, and aggregation of customer records.
2. Application log analysis — parsing, structuring, and deriving metrics (errors, latency, traffic) from application logs.
3. Visualization components — reusable chart/widget components composing into a dashboard view.

Goal: a single dashboard surfacing customer-derived business metrics alongside operational log metrics.

Delivery approach: milestone-based, with every task decomposed to a complexity of 6 or below so each is independently executable.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, visualization

tasks.name: M1: Foundation, Data Contracts & Metric Catalog
tasks.details:
Milestone container. Establishes the shared ground both data pipelines and the visualization layer build against: the metric definitions, canonical schemas, repo/tooling baseline, and test fixtures. Everything downstream is blocked on this.

Exit criteria: metric catalog approved, schemas locked, CI green on an empty skeleton, fixtures available for both sources.

tasks.name: M2: Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
tasks.details:
Milestone container. Full path from raw customer CSV files to query-ready customer metrics: ingestion, validation, normalization/deduplication, aggregation, and load.

Exit criteria: a customer CSV dropped into the landing zone appears as validated, deduplicated customer records plus computed customer metrics, with rejects quarantined and reported.

tasks.name: M3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
Milestone container. Turns raw application logs into structured operational metrics: ingestion, parsing, error classification, latency/traffic derivation, and storage of aggregated log metrics.

Exit criteria: application logs are parsed into structured events, error signatures are grouped, and error-rate / latency / traffic metrics are queryable over time windows.

tasks.name: M4: Visualization Components & Dashboard Assembly
tasks.details:
Milestone container. Builds the presentation layer: theming/layout, reusable chart primitives, a data-fetching layer over both metric stores, and composition of the customer and operations dashboard views.

Exit criteria: both dashboard views render live data from the customer and log metric stores using shared components, and are responsive at target screen sizes.

tasks.name: M5: Integration, Hardening & Launch
tasks.details:
Milestone container. Proves the three streams work together, validates performance against realistic volumes, and gets it running in production with observability and documentation.

Exit criteria: end-to-end test suite green, performance targets met on production-scale data, monitoring live, and a documented, reversible production rollout.

tasks.name: 1.1 Define metric catalog and KPI definitions
tasks.details:
Write the single source of truth for every number the dashboard will show. For each metric: business definition, formula, grain (customer/day/week), source system, owner, and acceptable freshness.

Must cover both families:
- Customer metrics: active customers, new vs returning, churn/retention cohorts, revenue per customer, segment breakdowns.
- Operational metrics: request volume, error rate, p95/p99 latency, top error signatures.

Include a semantic layer mapping each metric to its canonical field name so the viz layer and both pipelines cannot drift. Output: catalog doc + machine-readable metric definitions file.

Done when: reviewed with stakeholders, every dashboard widget traces to one catalog entry.

tasks.name: 1.2 Lock canonical schemas for customer, log event, and metric records
tasks.details:
Define versioned schemas that both pipelines and the dashboard API agree on:

1. CustomerRecord — identifier(s), attributes, segment, lifecycle dates, normalized types/nullability rules.
2. LogEvent — timestamp, level, service, message, stack trace, request id, latency, status code, plus an `unparsed` escape hatch.
3. MetricPoint — metric id (from catalog), dimensions, time bucket, value, source, ingestion batch id.

Include field-level docs, required vs optional, and a schema version field for forward compatibility. Publish as JSON Schema / typed models. Define the compatibility rule for schema changes (additive only within a major version).

tasks.name: 1.3 Scaffold repository, tooling, and CI pipeline
tasks.details:
Create the monorepo/skeleton both the data and visualization streams will build in. Includes package/module layout for pipelines vs. UI, formatter + linter, type checking, unit test runner, pre-commit hooks, and a CI pipeline that runs lint/typecheck/test on every PR.

Add a Dockerfile or equivalent local dev environment so pipelines and dashboard run consistently. Keep it a skeleton — no business logic. Done when CI is green on an empty skeleton and a new contributor can run the stack from the README.

tasks.name: 1.4 Build test fixtures and synthetic datasets for both sources
tasks.details:
Produce reproducible sample data so both pipelines can be developed without touching real customer data.

- Customer CSVs: a well-formed baseline, plus adversarial variants (missing headers, BOM, Windows line endings, embedded commas/quotes, mixed date formats, duplicate rows, unicode names, empty file, ragged rows).
- Application logs: JSON and plaintext lines, multiline stack traces, interleaved request ids, malformed lines, out-of-order timestamps, very long messages.

Commit small fixtures to the repo; generate large volumes with a seeded script for performance testing later. Done when fixtures are documented and seeded generator is deterministic.

tasks.name: 2.1 Build CSV ingestion reader with encoding and delimiter detection
tasks.details:
Implement the first stage of the customer pipeline: discover CSV files in the landing zone, read them robustly, and emit raw rows with source metadata.

Handle: BOM/UTF-8/UTF-16/Latin-1 detection, delimiter sniffing (comma/semicolon/tab), quoted fields with embedded delimiters and newlines, header normalization, and streaming reads so large files do not load fully into memory. Tag every row with file name, row number, and ingestion batch id for traceability.

Done when all well-formed and adversarial CSV fixtures from 1.4 parse or fail with an explicit, actionable error.

tasks.name: 2.2 Implement schema validation and reject quarantine
tasks.details:
Validate ingested rows against the CustomerRecord schema from 1.2. Keep valid rows flowing; route invalid rows to a quarantine store with the specific failure reason (missing required field, bad type, unparseable date, out-of-range value) and source coordinates.

Design it as row-level validation so one bad row never fails a whole file. Produce a per-batch report: rows read, accepted, rejected, and top rejection reasons. Define the policy for unknown extra columns (warn and keep vs. drop).

Done when a batch report is emitted for every ingestion and every rejection reason is individually asserted in tests.

tasks.name: 2.3 Normalize customer records and resolve duplicates
tasks.details:
Canonicalize validated rows and collapse multiple rows per real-world customer into one authoritative record.

Normalization: trim/case-fold names, standardize emails (lowercase, validate syntax), phone/address formats, ISO country codes, and consistent date/timezone handling. Exact-match dedupe on stable keys first; then a configurable fuzzy match (normalized email, name+dob, etc.) producing merge candidates.

Define precedence when duplicates disagree (most recent wins vs. most complete), keep a survivorship audit trail, and make merges reversible. Flag ambiguous matches for review rather than silently merging.

Done when duplicates in fixtures collapse to expected counts and the merge audit is queryable.

tasks.name: 2.4 Compute customer metrics and cohort aggregates
tasks.details:
Implement the metric logic from the catalog (1.1) over deduplicated customer records: active/new/returning counts, retention and churn cohorts by signup month, revenue per customer, and segment breakdowns.

Treat this as a pure transformation: deduplicated records in, MetricPoints out. Keep it deterministic and unit-testable with hand-computed expected values on small fixtures. Parameterize the time window rather than hardcoding dates, and handle partial-period edge cases explicitly.

Done when each customer metric has a unit test asserting exact expected values.

tasks.name: 2.5 Load customer records and metrics into the analytical store
tasks.details:
Persist deduplicated customer records and computed MetricPoints into the shared analytical store so the dashboard can query them.

Implement idempotent upserts keyed on customer id and (metric id, dimensions, time bucket) so re-running a batch does not double-count — this is the most common source of wrong dashboards. Add batch-level transactional semantics: a failed load leaves no partial state. Version rows by ingestion batch for traceability and rollback.

Done when re-running the same batch twice yields identical row counts and metric values.

tasks.name: 3.1 Build log source ingestion and format detection
tasks.details:
Read application logs from their source (files/log shipper/stream) and determine the format of each record before parsing.

Detect per-line or per-record: JSON vs. plaintext, common plaintext layouts (timestamp-level-service-message), multiline stack traces that must be joined to the preceding error line, and interleaved concurrent request streams. Handle large files by streaming and track offsets/checkpoints so a restart resumes rather than reprocesses.

Emit raw records with source metadata (file, offset, ingestion batch). Done when mixed-format fixtures are each correctly classified and multiline traces are reassembled intact.

tasks.name: 3.2 Parse raw log records into the canonical LogEvent schema
tasks.details:
Convert detected raw records into the LogEvent schema from 1.2: timestamp (normalized to UTC), level, service, message, exception type/stack, request/trace id, status code, and duration.

Write one parser adapter per format plus a timestamp-format fallback chain (ISO8601, epoch seconds/millis, common locale formats). Records that cannot be parsed must land in an `unparsed` bucket with the raw payload preserved — never silently dropped. Extract structured fields from message text with a conservative, documented regex set.

Done when every fixture line maps to either a fully populated LogEvent or a logged parse failure with a reason.

tasks.name: 3.3 Classify errors and group them into signatures
tasks.details:
Turn individual error events into groupings an operator can act on.

Normalize each error message into a stable signature by masking variable parts: UUIDs, numeric ids, timestamps, durations, IPs, file paths, and query parameters. Group by (service, exception type, signature) so "user 8821 not found" and "user 9202 not found" collapse together. Assign severity from level plus exception class, and detect first-seen / last-seen / occurrence-count per signature so the UI can show new vs. recurring errors.

Done when known fixtures collapse to the expected number of signatures and masking rules are covered by tests.

tasks.name: 3.4 Derive latency and traffic metrics over time windows
tasks.details:
Compute the operational metrics from the catalog (1.1) out of parsed LogEvents: request volume, throughput, error rate, and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) bucketed by minute/hour/day and by service/route as dimensions.

Use a percentile method that survives merging across buckets (t-digest, histogram buckets, or HDR sketch) rather than averaging pre-computed percentiles — averaging percentiles is statistically wrong and is a common dashboard bug. Handle sparse buckets and nulls explicitly.

Done when percentile output on a fixture with known distribution matches the hand-computed value within tolerance.

tasks.name: 3.5 Store log metrics with retention and rollup policy
tasks.details:
Persist log-derived MetricPoints and error signatures into the same analytical store used by the customer pipeline, using the identical MetricPoint contract from 1.2/2.5.

Define retention and rollup: keep fine-grained buckets for a short window, progressively roll up to hourly/daily for long-range views, and document the exact windows. Ensure queries over long ranges transparently select the right rollup table. Idempotent by (metric id, dimensions, bucket).

Done when a query for a 90-day range returns identically to the rolled-up source, and re-ingesting a batch does not change totals.

tasks.name: 4.1 Establish design tokens, theme, and responsive layout shell
tasks.details:
Create the visual and structural foundation all widgets inherit: color palette (including accessible, colorblind-safe categorical series), typography scale, spacing, elevation, and chart-specific tokens (grid, axis, tooltip).

Build the responsive dashboard shell: header, nav, filter bar container, and a 12-column grid that reflows between desktop/tablet/mobile. Include loading, empty, and error states as first-class components so every widget can reuse them.

Done when the shell renders at three breakpoints with placeholder cards and tokens are documented in a storybook or equivalent.

tasks.name: 4.2 Build core chart primitives (time series, bar, KPI tile)
tasks.details:
Implement three reusable, data-agnostic chart components: a time-series line/area chart, a categorical bar chart, and a KPI stat tile with trend/delta.

Each takes a typed props contract (series, dimensions, formatting) rather than fetching its own data, so it is pure and snapshot-testable. Cover interaction: hover tooltip with crosshair, legend toggle, and time-range brush on the time series. Handle edge cases that break naive charts: all-zero series, single data point, nulls/gaps, very long labels, and huge value ranges (axis formatting).

Done when each primitive renders from fixtures at all breakpoints and has tests for the edge cases above.

tasks.name: 4.3 Build the data table component
tasks.details:
Build the table used for drill-downs (customer lists, top error signatures): column definitions, client/server-side sorting, filtering, pagination or virtual scrolling for large result sets, and numeric/date cell formatting.

Include loading and empty states from 4.1, and a row-click hook so the table can drive cross-filtering of charts. Must stay responsive with 10k+ rows — use virtualization rather than rendering every row.

Done when it handles 10k rows smoothly, sorts and filters correctly, and edge cases (no results, single row, very wide cells) are tested.

tasks.name: 4.4 Build the dashboard data/API layer and global filter state
tasks.details:
Create the thin API layer between the metric store and the UI, plus the shared filter state that drives every widget.

API: a metric query endpoint taking metric id, dimensions, time range, and granularity — validating against the catalog definition, and returning series ready to hand to chart primitives. Add caching and request de-duplication so a page with 8 widgets does not fire 8 redundant queries.

State: a single global time range + segment/service filter, URL-synced so views are shareable, and debounced so rapid filter changes do not flood the API. Handle abort of in-flight requests on change.

Done when widgets read one filter source and a filter change refetches exactly once.

tasks.name: 4.5 Compose the customer analytics dashboard view
tasks.details:
Assemble the customer-facing view from the primitives: KPI row (active/new/returning customers, churn rate, revenue per customer), retention cohort heatmap or matrix, segment breakdown bar chart, and a customer drill-down table.

Wire all widgets to the shared filter state from 4.4 and the customer metrics from 2.4. Every widget reads from the catalog-backed definitions — no hardcoded metric logic in the UI. Include per-widget loading/empty/error states.

Done when the view renders live customer metrics, filters apply consistently to all widgets, and the numbers reconcile with 2.4's test expectations.

tasks.name: 4.6 Compose the operations / log analysis dashboard view
tasks.details:
Assemble the operational view: request volume over time, error-rate trend, latency percentile chart (p50/p95/p99), and a top-error-signatures table with occurrence counts and first/last seen.

Wire to log metrics from 3.4/3.5 and error signatures from 3.3 through the shared filter state. Add cross-filtering: clicking an error signature narrows the time-series charts to that signature. Make "unparsed records" visible somewhere so silent data loss is noticeable.

Done when the view renders live log metrics, cross-filtering works, and displayed values reconcile with 3.4's percentile tests.

tasks.name: 5.1 Write end-to-end integration tests across all three streams
tasks.details:
Prove the whole path works: CSV and log fixtures in, dashboard queries out, asserted against expected values.

Cover the seams where integration bugs live: batch boundaries, retries and idempotency, timezone handling across pipeline and UI, schema version compatibility, and filter-to-query translation. Include a golden-dataset test where the full pipeline is run and output metric values are compared to a committed expected snapshot, so unintended logic changes fail loudly.

Done when the suite runs in CI against the containerized stack and is green.

tasks.name: 5.2 Validate performance and load with production-scale data
tasks.details:
Use the seeded generator from 1.4 to produce production-scale CSV and log volumes, then measure and fix bottlenecks.

Establish and record targets before testing: ingestion throughput per file size, end-to-end pipeline latency, dashboard p95 query response, and dashboard first meaningful paint. Profile the slowest stage in each pipeline and the slowest dashboard query; address memory ceilings (streaming vs. load-all) and any N+1 query patterns in the API layer.

Done when documented targets are met and results are recorded with the test configuration that produced them.

tasks.name: 5.3 Set up monitoring, alerting, and operations runbooks
tasks.details:
Make the system observable in production: structured logs for both pipelines, stage-level metrics (files processed, rows rejected, parse failure rate, batch duration), and dashboard-side error tracking.

Define alerts that matter: pipeline stalled or failed, reject rate above threshold, parse failure rate above threshold, data freshness beyond SLA, and dashboard API error/latency spikes. Write runbooks for each alert with first diagnostic steps and rollback instructions.

Done when each alert fires in a staging test and has a linked runbook.

tasks.name: 5.4 Write documentation and user guide
tasks.details:
Document the system for its three audiences: operators (how to run pipelines, interpret batch rejects, respond to alerts), analysts (what each metric means, its grain and freshness, where it comes from), and engineers (architecture diagram, schema versions, how to add a metric end to end).

Include a "known limitations" section — parsing formats not covered, retention windows, and any metric approximations (e.g. sketch-based percentiles). Document the exact steps to add a new CSV source or a new log format.

Done when a new team member can onboard from the docs alone and the metric definitions reconcile with the catalog.

tasks.name: 5.5 Build deployment pipeline and execute phased rollout
tasks.details:
Automate deployment of pipelines and dashboard through staging to production, then roll out in phases.

Pipeline: build artifacts, run migrations for the analytical store, deploy to staging automatically on merge, require manual approval for production. Make store migrations backward-compatible (expand/contract) so pipeline and UI versions can deploy independently.

Rollout: backfill one historical period first and verify against known figures with stakeholders, then enable scheduled ingestion, then open the dashboard to a small pilot group before full access. Define rollback triggers and rehearse the rollback once.

Done when production is live, backfill reconciles, and rollback has been exercised successfully.
